summary.registry_lookup: ISS-0764 is the direct prior entry with identical symptoms -- same file (lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex), same defect description (raw string-list membership check on conn.assigns.auth_context.roles instead of Authorization.roles_from_strings/1 for the PLATFORM_ADMIN exemption), same MINOR severity, same fix direction, filed by REVIEWER during WF03-ISS0736-20260921 on 2026-09-21. ISS-0764 was never resolved (status: open at filing); ISS-0808 was opened 2026-09-24 referencing ISS-0764 in its 'related' field, indicating the issue was re-triaged/re-queued rather than a recurrence of a previously shipped fix. No severity escalation required -- this is the same original open finding, not a recurrence after a fix that failed to hold. Additionally, ISS-0774 and ISS-0775 touch Authorization.roles_from_strings/1 and role-domain separation but concern entirely different code paths (tenant_role.kind filtering, OIDC claim write path) -- not the same root cause.
summary.root_cause: lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex, pre-fix state (parent of commit 97c50b5d): (1) Module attribute @platform_admin was declared as the string "PLATFORM_ADMIN" (line ~62 in pre-fix tree, confirmed via `git show 97c50b5d^`); (2) The PLATFORM_ADMIN exemption check at lines 92-95 read raw_roles directly from conn.assigns.auth_context.roles (a list of raw strings from the JWT/auth context) and tested `@platform_admin not in roles` -- a plain string-list membership check, never passing the roles through Authorization.roles_from_strings/1. Every other authorization consumer in the codebase (Letflow.Plugs.Authorize, policy evaluators) converts the raw-string roles list through Authorization.roles_from_strings/1 first, which maps recognized strings to a closed atom set (e.g. "PLATFORM_ADMIN" -> :PLATFORM_ADMIN). The plug's raw check happened to produce the same result today because roles_from_strings/1 uses a plain string-match clause (`role_from_string("PLATFORM_ADMIN") -> :PLATFORM_ADMIN`) and the representation has not changed. The risk is silent future divergence: if roles_from_strings/1 ever changes normalization (case folding, aliasing, a role rename), the plug's hard-coded raw string comparison would go stale with no test or compiler guard catching it.
summary.why_tests_missed: No test in test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs exercised the PLATFORM_ADMIN exemption path in a way that discriminated between 'raw string comparison' and 'routed through roles_from_strings/1'. Both code paths produce the identical runtime result for the unmodified PLATFORM_ADMIN string representation -- a test passing the string "PLATFORM_ADMIN" as a role would pass whether the check used `@platform_admin not in roles` (string) or the atom `:PLATFORM_ADMIN not in roles` (atom, after conversion). The divergence is only detectable if the test uses a representation that roles_from_strings/1 normalizes but the raw string check would not recognize (e.g., a case-variant or an alias). No such test existed; the regression tests added in commit 97c50b5d (3 tests: PLATFORM_ADMIN exempt, PROCESS_OPERATOR rejected, unknown role rejected) were the first to structurally require roles_from_strings/1 to be called, because @platform_admin is now the atom :PLATFORM_ADMIN -- if the conversion is removed, PLATFORM_ADMIN callers get 403, which the 'PLATFORM_ADMIN exempt' test catches.
summary.fix_needed: Replace raw string comparison with Authorization.roles_from_strings/1 and use atom :PLATFORM_ADMIN -- already done in 97c50b5d
